trust_decision.summary: Decided per logr.MarshalLog implementation: configured trace-exporter endpoint/URL state must not be emitted by any marshaled log value, and this is enforced only at the exporters and sdk/trace processors, never in the config parsers or the exporters' own logf calls.

landing_point.why: The advisory says endpoint configuration leaks in info logs; this is the only info-level log that marshals the TracerProvider config, and every MarshalLog in sdk/trace and the trace exporters hangs off it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Zipkin is a wholly separate exporter with its own URL handling and no OTLP config; a solver can argue the advisory is about OTLP exporter endpoint configuration and that zipkin's URL in MarshalLog is the only way its target is identifiable.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The internal logs must still identify the component and keep the non-secret diagnostics: Type names ('otlptracehttp', 'otlptracegrpc', 'zipkin', 'SimpleSpanProcessor') and the batch processor's BatchSpanProcessorOptions, following the precedent already set at provider.go:57-58 (fmt.Sprintf("%T", sampler)); a blanket redaction returning nil or an empty MarshalLog payload breaks the logr.Marshaler contract and the log.

O6_input_shapes: endpoint as plain host:port (otlptracegrpc/otlptracehttp Endpoint field)
endpoint as user:pass@host:port (the credential shape used in the fix's own test literals)
full collector URL with userinfo and query token (zipkin.New)
the companion Insecure bool next to Endpoint
exporter value logged directly as a logr key/value vs nested two levels deep through TracerProviderOption -> SpanProcessor -> SpanExporter
interface-typed field (Client, SpanExporter) vs concrete string/bool fields inside MarshalLog

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Zipkin ExportSpans logs the raw collector URL (userinfo and query token included) at info level via e.logf on every export, and errf embeds it in logged error messages
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It goes to the exporter's opt-in user-supplied logger (WithLogger/WithLogr), not the internal global logger the advisory names, so it reads as a different sink.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as a fix site, different function and a hot export path the fix's test never calls

O8_uncovered_routes.route: OTLP/HTTP client passes the raw configured endpoint into self-observability BaseAttrs, which debug-logs it verbatim when it does not parse as host:port
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Experimental self-observability is off unless OTEL_GO_X_OBSERVABILITY is set and it is a debug-level parse-failure path, not the exporter config info log.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: internal package one level below the fixed client.go, reached from client.Start

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WithEndpointURL logs the raw URL value on url.Parse failure (duplicated in both OTLP trace transport copies)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It only fires on a malformed endpoint at option-construction time, so it is an error path rather than exporter configuration logging.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: internal/otlpconfig copy in each transport module; identical line at exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc/internal/otlpconfig/options.go:283

O8b_injection_room.sibling: PeriodicReader.MarshalLog still returns the Exporter interface value, the same shape the fix removed from the two span processors
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The metric exporters were already sanitized one release earlier (exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp/exporter.go:139-141), so a maintainer adding a MeterProvider-created log or a third-party metric exporter would produce exactly this leak.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Log-exporter config loaders log the raw endpoint URL on parse failure, and the log exporters implement no MarshalLog at all
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The log exporters mirror the metric/trace exporters file for file; a maintainer copying the trace fix forward, or the trace fix being back-ported, lands here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another trace SpanExporter MarshalLog that exists and is reached by the same TracerProvider config log, currently exposing only a harmless bool
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Adding a configured output path or destination field to stdouttrace is a natural extension and would leak the same way.

O9_family: sensitive information exposure through logging (CWE-200 / CWE-532)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.0; 28 separate go.mod modules with no go.work, so each changed module is built and tested independently
O10_build.project_tests: exporters/otlp/otlptrace/exporter_test.go, exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc/client_test.go, exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp/client_internal_test.go, exporters/zipkin/zipkin_test.go, sdk/trace/provider_test.go - all offline, no collector or network needed for the MarshalLog assertions

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete or stringify the Endpoint field in the two OTLP trace client MarshalLog methods only, verify with otlptracehttp/otlptracegrpc, and stop there.

out_of_scope_notes: The metric exporters already return a Type-only MarshalLog (exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp/exporter.go:139-141, otlpmetricgrpc/exporter.go:168-170), so that sibling was fixed before this pinned commit and is not part of this advisory.
Log-signal exporters (otlploghttp/otlploggrpc) still log raw endpoint URLs from their config loaders, but they are outside this trace-only advisory.
sdk/metric/periodic_reader.go:444 still marshals the Exporter interface value, outside this advisory's trace protection.
zipkin.New returns errors that embed the collector URL (exporters/zipkin/zipkin.go:100,103), an error return rather than a log write.
